transcript:
Header:
Date/Time: 2026-07-07 09:00 PT
Duration: 52 minutes
Recording ID: ff-recording-20260707-arch-01
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Archimedes CTO), Leo Park (ML Engineer), Rafael Gomez (Infra Lead)

Summary:
Quick discovery focused on migration from OpenAI-hosted models to Redwood Dedicated; compatibility concerns (vLLM/TGI), eval parity, security and VPC requirements, and next steps for benchmarking and pricing.

Topics:
- current stack and pain points
- eval parity and tokenization differences
- runtime compatibility vLLM/TGI and quantization
- security (SOC2, KMS, SSO) and VPC peering
- pricing and pilot/POC scope

Transcript:
[00:00] Samir (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining — Samir here from Redwood, with Lena on the call. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Maya (Archimedes): Good, thanks. Sorry we're a little late, been shuffling meetings.
[00:10] Samir: No problem at all. We'll keep to about 45-60 minutes, we have your agenda from the form but feel free to add anything.
[00:18] Leo (Archimedes): Thanks. Our main ask is, we run most stuff on OpenAI today for generation and embeddings, but cost and latency at scale are killing us. Want to understand dedicated options and how close outputs will be — eval parity — and also whether our current vLLM/TGI stack will map to Redwood.
[00:33] Lena (Redwood): Great, that's exactly what we do. Quick high level: Redwood Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools with model variants we validate; we support running open models and can route to hosted or private. We also do kernel/quantization selection to hit latency SLOs.
[00:46] Rafael (Archimedes): A few specifics from infra: we need VPC peering or private link, audit logs forwarded to our SIEM, KMS integration for key custody, and we prefer region-us-west-2. Can you do all that on Dedicated?
[00:58] Lena: Yes, Dedicated supports VPC peering, private control plane options, and KMS/HSM integrations. We also provide audit logs; we can forward to your SIEM. We'll share the VPC checklist.
[01:08] Maya: Also SOC2 and ISO?
[01:11] Samir: Redwood has SOC2 Type II; Lena will share the attestation link.
[01:15] Maya: Cool.
[01:17] Leo: About compatibility — we use vLLM on top of a lot of our inference and some TGI wrappers. Are your runtimes compatible? I saw notes about KV cache, batching optimizations — will we have to rewrite inference code?
[01:28] Lena: Short answer: usually no major rewrites. We support common model formats (HF/ggml/whatever) and provide a compatible API layer. For vLLM/TGI specifically, there are nuances: context window handling and tokenization differences can cause subtle output drift. We run eval parity tests during onboarding.
[01:43] Leo: Tokenization differences, yeah — we've seen that cause scoring differences with our eval sets.
[01:48] Samir: Right, so two things we propose — one, a small parity bench that runs your eval prompts against the OpenAI baseline and our Dedicated setup; two, we can tune quantization (INT8/FP16) and kernel choices to match quality/latency tradeoffs.
[02:02] Rafael: What's the expected latency improvement if we go Dedicated vs staying on OpenAI? Also cost per token ballpark?
[02:10] Samir: Depends on model and shard sizes, but for large gen models we've seen p95 latency drop by 20-50% when colocated and with optimized kernels; cost can drop 30-70% per token depending on steady throughput and batching. We'll give three sizing options (small/medium/large) with modeled cost.
[02:26] Maya: And fallback — if Dedicated capacity is saturated, can requests failover to Redwood hosted or degrade gracefully?
[02:32] Lena: Yes, routing policies allow fallback to hosted or to a smaller model variant. We can set canary rollouts and automatic fallback to keep you online.
[02:40] Leo: On the eval parity bench: can you run with our vLLM/TGI stack so we get a like-for-like compare? We worry about changes in pre/post-processing.
[02:49] Lena: We can spin up a Dedicated environment that mirrors your stack, including similar tokenizer and pre/post-processing. Some parts of vLLM are runtime-specific but we support integrations and can run the bench with your code or our harness, whichever you prefer.
[03:02] Rafael: Network egress — our data rules restrict sending any PII off our VPC. Is there an air-gapped or fully private option?
[03:09] Samir: For sensitive workloads we offer Private deployments (VPC/on-prem) with a private control plane and optional air-gapped on-prem. For Dedicated we also offer strong isolation and you can opt to keep data in-region and controls on KMS; we'll go over the data flow in the security notes.
[03:22] Maya: Good. Also curious about model versions and rolling — can we pin versions? We need reproducibility.
[03:28] Lena: Absolutely; model versioning, pinning, and rollout policies are supported. You can pin a model artifact and control canary percentages.
[03:33] Leo: One concern: we use a few custom adapter layers and low-level optimizations in vLLM — will Redwood's runtime break any of that?
[03:41] Lena: There may be edge cases. For heavy customizations that patch vLLM internals, we recommend running the parity tests and a short POC where you provide the adapter so we can validate. We have an engineering support path for those scenarios.
[03:54] Maya: How long does a POC usually take? If we want to validate parity and perf, what's realistic?
[03:59] Samir: For a scoped POC with your eval set and a single model family, 2-4 weeks is typical: week 1 provisioning & onboarding, week 2 benching and tuning, week 3 quality review and ops integration. Could be shorter if you're ready.
[04:13] Rafael: On logging — do you provide token-level traces? We need to map costs to routes.
[04:19] Lena: We provide per-token cost breakdowns, traces per request, and route/model dashboards in the console. We also give export to your analytics pipeline.
[04:28] Leo: Any gotchas moving from OpenAI — like differences in stop token handling or sampling seeds? We've had nondeterministic diffs in evaluations.
[04:36] Samir: Yes, sampling and RNG can vary. For deterministic runs we recommend using greedy or fixed seeds if available; we'll document exact runtime params. Part of parity is matching temp, topk/top-p, and seeding where possible.
[04:48] Maya: On compliance — SSO, RBAC, and audit logs — we need SAML/SSO and fine-grained RBAC for different teams.
[04:56] Lena: Supported. We integrate with major IdPs (SAML/Okta), provide RBAC in the console, and can forward audit logs. We'll send the RBAC spec.
[05:05] Leo: For throughput testing — can we run a continuous stream to mimic our production traffic? We have spiky bursts; autoscale behavior is important.
[05:14] Samir: Yes, Dedicated has configurable autoscaling and burst capacity. For spikes we recommend configuring a burst pool and we can simulate your workload during the POC.
[05:23] Rafael: Any limitations with model sizes? We want to run some 70B and a couple 13B models, and a long context 32k.
[05:30] Lena: We support common 70B/13B variants and long-context models. For 32k contexts we'll pick kernels and KV cache strategies that avoid memory blowouts; may require different VM types. We'll include that in sizing.
[05:42] Maya: What about quantization? We saw quality regressions with some INT8 profiles.
[05:47] Lena: It depends on model. We do model-level quantization recommendations and A/B quality checks. Sometimes INT8 is fine, sometimes you need FP16 or custom quant. We'll run a few profiles in the POC.
[05:57] Leo: Do you keep a model catalog? If we want to upgrade to new open model releases how do you handle compatibility?
[06:03] Samir: We maintain a catalog with validated profiles and performance notes; upgrades are controlled and we support rollback. You can also bring your own model artifact.
[06:10] Maya: Ok, next steps?
[06:13] Samir: Recap — we'll do: 1) send pricing and dedicated sizing options, 2) Lena shares security artifacts (SOC2, KMS, VPC checklist), 3) Archimedes to share eval prompts and a small sample dataset for parity, 4) schedule a 2-4 week POC/benchmark window week of 7/13.
[06:28] Maya: That sounds right. One ask: can we have an SE session where Lena walks our ML team through the tokenization and exact runtime params?
[06:35] Lena: Absolutely, we can schedule a technical deep dive after the POC kickoff.
[06:40] Rafael: If we decide on Dedicated, what's the SLA like?
[06:44] Samir: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and latency targets; we'll include SLA language in the contract options.
[06:50] Leo: Any legal / data residency paperwork we should expect?
[06:53] Samir: We'll include standard DPA and region controls; legal can pre-send a template if you'd like.
[06:59] Maya: Great.
[07:01] Samir: Cool, we'll follow up with the materials — Lena do you want to call out any items?
[07:06] Lena: I'll share the SOC2 link, KMS integration notes, VPC peering checklist, and the POC runbook. Also I'll propose a concrete bench harness and ask for the eval set.
[07:16] Maya: Perfect, thanks both.
[07:18] Samir: Thanks all, we'll send those items and get a calendar invite for POC kickoff.
[07:22] End of recording
